key_insight: A deep-learning electronic frailty index built from structured and free-text EHR data can identify frailty risk across adulthood, not just in older adults.
clinical_relevance: This approach may improve early risk stratification for mortality, infection, fractures, and healthcare use, especially when frailty is still mild or not yet clinically obvious.
method: Analyzed longitudinal EHRs from 193,629 people aged 35-103 in Central Finland (2010-2023).
Built a 53-item eFI using diagnosis codes, lab tests, and items extracted from clinical notes via deep-learning NLP.
Compared prediction against Hospital Frailty Risk Score (HFRS) and Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) using Cox and count models.
evidence_signal: Severe frailty was associated with markedly higher risks of mortality, severe infections, fractures, and healthcare utilization, and the eFI outperformed HFRS and CCI across outcomes.
watch_item: Performance was demonstrated in one regional health system, so external validation and careful integration of free-text NLP extraction are needed before broader deployment.
paper_title: A next-generation electronic frailty index leveraging deep learning on unstructured health records extends risk prediction across the full frailty spectrum
